comments.content: `config_path` was widened from concrete `&AppHandle` to generic `<R: tauri::Runtime>`. This is consistent with `db::data_dir`, but it is a **potentially source-breaking change** for any external caller who typed `config_path` as a function pointer (`fn(&AppHandle) -> PathBuf`) or matched its signature with a non-generic alias. Internal callers all infer `R = tauri::Wry` and compile fine. If downstream crates depend on the old concrete signature, this change is a breaking API change — worth a CHANGELOG note. Also note the inconsistency: most other public helpers in this file (`load_config`, `read_bypass_llm_switch`, `migrate_legacy_key`, `add_allowed_dir`, `update_config_file`) still take the concrete `&AppHandle`. Only `read_memory_control` was made generic. Either both should be generic (for parity with the requirement that injection runs on a generic-runtime task executor) or both should remain concrete — pick one and stay consistent.

`read_memory_control` is `pub` but is not re-exported via `pub use io::{...}` in `bot/config/mod.rs:46`, nor added to the `bot.rs` facade re-export list (lines 64-114). The doc comment at `mod.rs:7` states all external callers must use the `crate::bot::<item>` facade and not access `crate::bot::config::<item>` directly. The current caller (`memory::mod.rs:73`) does exactly that — accesses `crate::bot::config::io::read_memory_control` directly, breaking the facade contract. Add it to both re-export lists (or downgrade it to `pub(crate)` and update the comment if it's intentionally internal-only).

The new test `read_memory_control_defaults_none_and_honors_explicit_block` (mod.rs:502) does not exercise partial-field deserialization — e.g. `{"memoryControl":{"injectionEnabled":false}}` where `autoWriteEnabled` is absent. Since `MemoryControl` derives `#[serde(default)]`, the missing field should default to `true`. Without this case, the "missing field defaults to open" guarantee is asserted only implicitly; an explicit case protects against future serde-attribute drift.

`read_memory_control_at` parses the entire `BotConfig` (baseUrl, model, key slots, MCP servers, evolution, etc.) on every gate check just to extract `memory_control`. This runs on every chat turn (`injection_block` at the start of every message) and on every model tool call to `remember_fact`/`record_lesson`. For a toggle that's read far more often than written, consider either: (a) parsing as `serde_json::Value` and plucking only `memoryControl`, (b) caching the parsed control in a `OnceLock<Mutex<Option<MemoryControl>>>` with file mtime invalidation, or (c) at minimum documenting that the existing pattern mirrors `read_bypass_llm_switch` which has the same trade-off.

Within the same module, `read_bypass_llm_switch(app: &AppHandle)` uses the concrete `AppHandle` alias while `read_memory_control(app: &tauri::AppHandle<R>)` is generic over `R`. Same trade-off (generic lets the test in `llm_integration.rs` pass `tauri::AppHandle<tauri::test::MockRuntime>`), but the asymmetry will confuse future readers. Either make `read_bypass_llm_switch` generic too, or add a one-line comment here noting the deliberate divergence.

Comment claims "纯函数，可测" for `injection_enabled`/`auto_write_enabled`, which is true for these two predicates. But the gate wrappers `injection_allowed`/`auto_write_allowed` (defined at lines 52-58 below) are private and take `tauri::AppHandle<R>`, so they cannot be unit-tested without a mock runtime — only exercised via the integration test in `llm_integration.rs::memory_gate_scenarios_injection_and_auto_write`. Consider clarifying the comment to distinguish the pure predicates from the I/O wrappers, or making the wrappers `pub(crate)` and accepting `Option<&MemoryControl>` so the file-read part is fully testable in isolation.

`control_of_view` maps every config-read failure (I/O error, permission error, parse error) to `None` = "all on" with zero logging. If the user's toggle silently doesn't take effect because of a permission denied / JSON corruption, they have no way to diagnose it. The `memory_control` field is a user-visible privacy-relevant setting — at minimum, distinguish "field missing (legit default)" from "config present but unreadable" and emit a one-line `eprintln!` or `audit_event!` warn when the file exists but reading/parsing fails. The `read_memory_control_at` test at `confirms the same behavior; a log there would surface real issues without breaking the "门禁绝不能弄挂聊天" guarantee.

[high] Race condition on shared DB between baseline capture and final count. Scenario 3 reads `load_all(&conn).len()` twice with two tool calls in between, but the test comment itself notes that `target/debug/deps/`'s `wmessage.db` is shared by all parallel test processes. Any sibling worker that writes/deletes rows between these two reads will change the count and produce a spurious "门禁关闭时不得写入" failure even though the gate logic is correct. Mitigation: instead of `assert_eq!(final_len, baseline)`, snapshot the IDs seen at baseline and assert that none of those IDs disappear and no new IDs (with the test's distinguishing attributes) appear — or wrap both reads in a `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`/rollback transaction on a dedicated connection so the comparison is isolated from concurrent writers.

[medium] Cleanup is best-effort and skipped on any panic/early-exit, defeating the purpose of merging scenarios to avoid shared-state pollution. The trailing `remove_file`, `delete_by_ids`, and `delete_by_key_tag` only run on the success path; if any assertion above panics, the shared `bot-config.json` (with `memoryControl: {injectionEnabled, autoWriteEnabled}` values) and the seeded rows are left in place for every parallel nextest worker, re-introducing the exact contamination this test is trying to mitigate. Wrap the test body in a Drop guard or RAII helper that runs cleanup unconditionally (e.g., `let _guard = MemoryControlCleanup { app: &app, seed: SEED_CONTENT, key: "测试键" };`), or use `scopeguard` / a manual `struct ... { conn, ... } impl Drop` so cleanup runs on the unwind path.

[medium] Silent error swallowing in cleanup hides real I/O / SQLite failures and can leak shared state. `let _ = std::fs::remove_file(...)` and `let _ = wmessage_lib::memory::store::delete_by_key_tag(&conn, "测试键")` discard every error class (NotFound vs PermissionDenied vs DbBusy vs DB locked); a real error during teardown will silently leave the shared DB polluted for every parallel worker, while the test still reports green. At minimum `eprintln!` (or `tracing::warn!` if the crate has it) on `Err`, and ideally propagate non-NotFound variants so a permission/lock failure is observable.

comments.content: `sqlite3.Connection`'s context manager only commits or rolls back the transaction — it does NOT close the connection. Every `with get_db() as conn:` in this file (9 places) leaks a file descriptor and a SQLite connection for the lifetime of the request handler. In a long-running service this can exhaust FDs or hit SQLite's per-process lock limit. Use an explicit factory that yields a connection inside a `try/finally`, or wrap with `closing(sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH))`.
comments.existing_code:
def get_db() -> sqlite3.Connection:
    conn = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    return conn

comments.content: `hash(pkey)` is not stable across restarts — Python seeds `str.__hash__` per process (PYTHONHASHSEED randomization), so the comment "稳定且可区分" is wrong: the fallback color for every provider will change on each restart, causing visible UI flicker. Use a deterministic hash (e.g., `hashlib.blake2b(pkey.encode(), digest_size=4).hexdigest()[:8]`) or pin `PYTHONHASHSEED`.

comments.content: `httpx.get` is a blocking synchronous call invoked from `async def lifespan`. Synchronous HTTP inside an async context stalls the event loop for up to 10 seconds during startup, delaying any concurrent awaits. Use `httpx.AsyncClient` and `await client.get(...)`, or run the sync call in `asyncio.to_thread(...)`.

comments.content:
`Err(_) => report.skipped += 1` lumps every `rusqlite::Error` / store failure (schema drift, I/O failure, locked DB, corruption) into the same "skipped" bucket as the legitimate `RejectedFull` / `RefusedForeignMerge` outcomes. A user importing a file that triggers a real storage error would see only `skipped: N` with no diagnostic — indistinguishable from normal input rejection. Either propagate the first error out of `import_core` (so the Tauri command surfaces it), or split the report into `skipped` and a separate `errors` channel, and at minimum `eprintln!("[mem_import] insert_item failed: {e}")` before counting.

Verify: `store::insert_item` (store.rs:247) returns `Result<(InsertOutcome, Vec<String>), String>` — the `String` carries actionable context that is being thrown away here, while every other caller in this crate preserves it (memory/mod.rs record_lesson_core → `format!("失败：{e}")`, remember_fact → same).

Missing ARIA switch semantics: this toggle button uses `aria-label` but lacks `role="switch"` and `aria-checked={...}`. The project's accessibility standard — enforced by `SettingsPage.test.tsx` (which asserts `getByRole("switch", ...)` + `toHaveAttribute("aria-checked", ...)` for the vendor toggle) and implemented in `src/components/Toggle/Toggle.tsx` (lines 40-42) — expects binary on/off controls to expose both attributes so screen readers announce them as toggles and convey the current state. For a privacy-sensitive control, this is especially worth getting right.

              aria-label="聊天注入记忆"
              className={`shrink-0 min-w-[76px] px-4 py-1.5 text-sm text-[var(--t3)] ${
                config.memoryControl.injectionEnabled ? "nm-inset" : "nm-outset"
              }`}

Only the field name, title, description, and aria-label differ. Extracting a small local helper (e.g., a `MemoryPermissionToggle` component or `renderMemoryPermissionToggle` function taking `{ field, title, description }`) would eliminate the duplication and ensure any future change (such as adding `role="switch"`/`aria-checked`, a tooltip, or a third permission) only needs to be made in one place.

comments.content: Optimistic update without rollback: `setConfig(next)` runs before `await saveConfig(next)`, but the boolean return value of `saveConfig` is discarded. `saveConfig` (line 644) catches backend failures (network error, schema rejection, write conflict) and returns `false` without calling `loadConfig()`, so the local React state keeps the toggled value while the backend keeps the old one — silent UI/backend divergence. This is the same pattern as the pre-existing `setConsolidation`/`toggleTavily`/`toggleBrave`/`setPermMode`, but for a privacy-sensitive control (`autoWriteEnabled` directly affects whether the model is allowed to write memories, `injectionEnabled` is the privacy master switch) silent divergence is more concerning. Capture the original `config` reference and roll back when `saveConfig` returns `false`.

Synchronous file I/O on the async runtime: `read_memory_control` runs `std::fs::read_to_string` directly. `injection_allowed` invokes it from `injection_block` (async) BEFORE `spawn_blocking`, so the file read happens on the async executor thread, not in a blocking pool. On a slow disk or contended FS, this can stall chat turns. Consider wrapping the read inside the existing `spawn_blocking` closure (e.g. pass `MemoryControl` lookup into the same blocking task) or adding `tokio::fs::read_to_string` if the project ever moves to tokio, to keep the async runtime responsive.

Test coverage gap (distinct from confirmed finding #4): the test only verifies `Some(MemoryControl { injection_enabled: false, auto_write_enabled: true })`. It does not cover: (a) `{"memoryControl":{"autoWriteEnabled":false}}` alone (auto_write gate flip), (b) `{"memoryControl":{}}` (empty object — with struct-level `#[serde(default)]` this should deserialize to `Some(MemoryControl::default())`, distinct from `memoryControl: null` → None), (c) `{"memoryControl":null}` (explicit null, must be None). Add these cases to lock the merge-with-default semantics so future refactors of `MemoryControl` don't change observable behavior.

Pattern violation: `mem_import` calls `embed::embed_text(text)` from inside the `lock_db()` critical section (the reembed closure is invoked inside `import_core` while the lock is held on line 434). Embedding is blocking ONNX inference — `embed::embed_text` is synchronous (memory/embed.rs:162) and lazy-loads the model on first call. For a large import with many items lacking vectors this holds the single-writer `DB_WRITE_LOCK` for the entire model-inference duration, blocking every other write path (chat-time `remember_fact` / `record_lesson` / `mem_update` / `mem_delete`).

The module doc at line 11 explicitly states the discipline is "嵌入在持锁前算" and `tool_record_lesson` in memory/mod.rs:596-601 follows it (line 597: `let emb = embed::embed_text(&lesson);` runs BEFORE line 598's lock acquisition). `mem_list` (panel.rs:223-227) and `mem_update` (panel.rs:245-246) also follow it.

Fix shape: pre-compute embeddings for items lacking vectors BEFORE acquiring `lock_db()` (collect items needing reembed, compute all vectors in one pass while unlocked, then acquire the lock and call a `import_core` variant that takes pre-computed embeddings). Keep the `&dyn Fn(...)` reembed hook for tests, but in the production path never call it inside the lock.

Lock held during full-dump JSON serialization. `export_core` builds the entire `MemExportFile` and runs `serde_json::to_string_pretty` over every item (including 512-dim embedding vectors) INSIDE the `lock_db()` block (line 413-418). For a large memory dump this serializes the full corpus (~1MB+ once you include embeddings) to a `String` inside the critical section, blocking all other writers. Only `load_all` strictly needs the lock; serialization and `std::fs::write` (which is already correctly placed after the lock drops on line 419) can move outside.

Fix shape: change the locked block to just return `Vec<MemItem>`, then call `export_core` and `std::fs::write` after `_g` drops. This naturally fixes issue 4 below as a side effect (no need to round-trip through JSON just to recover the count).

Unnecessary round-trip serialization. `export_core` returns a JSON `String`; that string is written to disk on line 419; then the same string is re-parsed via `serde_json::from_str::<MemExportFile>` on line 421 to recover the value to return to the caller. The justification in the comment ("避免再持锁查一次库") is moot — `export_core` already has the `MemExportFile` in hand before serializing.

Fix shape: change `export_core` to return `Result<(MemExportFile, String), String>` (or split into `build_export_file` + a thin serialize helper), then write the `String` and return the `MemExportFile` directly. Eliminates a redundant allocation, an extra full-corpus parse, and removes the "向本文字列回读校验" check which only catches serde_json bugs.

Cross-crate error category leak. The outer `.map_err(CommandError::DbError)` (line 426) is applied to the inner `Result<MemExportFile, String>`, but the inner `String` can carry file-write failures ("写入导出文件失败：...") and round-trip parse failures, not just DB errors. `CommandError` presumably has more specific variants for IO / parse failures. Same applies to `mem_import` at line 440 (file-read failure mapped to `DbError`) and the `mem_export` / `mem_import` "线程 join 失败" already correctly mapped to generic `CommandError::from`. Map file-system / serialization failures to the appropriate variants so the frontend can present them with the right category.

        .map_err(CommandError::DbError)

comments.content: Synchronous file I/O on the async runtime: `read_memory_control` performs `std::fs::read_to_string` directly. `injection_allowed` (memory/mod.rs:77) invokes it from the async `injection_block` BEFORE `spawn_blocking`, so the file read happens on the async executor thread, not in a blocking pool. On a slow disk or FS contention, this can stall chat turns. Consider folding the memory-control lookup into the existing `spawn_blocking` closure (pass a oneshot/channel into the blocking task, or read into a precomputed value there), so the file I/O never runs on the async executor.

Test's `seed_memory` calls `ensure_table` redundantly — `insert_item` already calls `ensure_table` internally. Minor, but the explicit call can mislead readers into thinking `insert_item` doesn't ensure the table.

Scenario 2's assertion `block.contains("## 记忆") && block.contains(SEED_CONTENT)` is necessary because the shared DB may have unrelated memories, but it only checks substring presence. The block might still be considered correct even if seed memory was added to the WRONG section (e.g., pinned vs. related), or if the ranking has a bug that affects content inclusion. Consider asserting on block structure (e.g., `block.contains("- [fact]")` or `block.matches(SEED_CONTENT).count() >= 1`) to narrow the regression surface.

Error response is returned with HTTP 200. Per REST conventions, error responses should use 4xx/5xx status codes so clients (and intermediaries like proxies, monitoring) can distinguish failures via `response.status_code` alone. Raise `HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=...)` or return `JSONResponse(..., status_code=400)` instead.

comments.content: `httpx.get(...).json()` does not check the HTTP status code. If models.dev returns 4xx/5xx with an HTML error page (common for 502/503 from gateways), `.json()` raises `JSONDecodeError` and the sync fails with a confusing stack. If the upstream returns a JSON error payload (e.g. `{"error": "..."}`), the code will iterate it as a dict of providers and either produce nonsense rows or crash deeper in the loop. Call `response.raise_for_status()` before `.json()`.
comments.suggestion_code:
response = httpx.get(MODELS_DEV_API, timeout=10)
    response.raise_for_status()
    data = response.json()

comments.content: 在对话框弹出前就 setIoMsg("")，会导致用户取消 save/open 时静默清掉之前已经显示的成功/失败提示（例如「已导出 3 条记忆」点导入后取消就消失了）。清除时机应推迟到确认拿到 path 之后再做，避免误吞前一条状态。建议把 setIoMsg("") 移到 `if (!path) return;` 之后。
同上：importMemories 在对话框弹出前 setIoMsg("")，用户取消 open 时也会静默清掉前一条状态。建议把 setIoMsg("") 移到 `if (!path) return;` 之后，与 exportMemories 行为一致。

`mem_import` 没有限制 `path` 的范围/形态。`path: String` 由前端 `plugin-dialog` 取值（用户选的本地路径），但前端任何代码都能 invoke 任意路径——读 `/etc/passwd` / `%APPDATA%/Microsoft/...` 等敏感文件都不会被 Rust 侧任何检查挡住。`mem_export` 同理：可写任意路径覆盖系统/用户关键文件。建议至少做以下任一：(a) `std::path::Path::new(&path).canonicalize()` 后验证是用户可写目录（家目录/桌面/下载等白名单）；(b) 校验扩展名（`.json`）+ 文件大小上限防 OOM（同 `PayloadTooLarge` 1MB 上限同款）。`workspace_import` 也是裸 `String` 路径，本批可一起拍板。

`import_core` 不校验 `kind` / `source` 字段：恶意/手工编辑过的 JSON 可以塞 `kind: "magic"` 或 `source: "garbage"` 入库，直接破坏数据完整性契约（`EDITABLE_KINDS` 白名单 / `is_protected` 的 `source == "user_stated"`）。`update_core` 对两个字段都做了白名单/语义校验，导入路径却绕过——同一数据契约两套口径。建议：(a) `kind` 走 `EDITABLE_KINDS` 白名单，未知值计入 `skipped`；(b) `source` 走 `{"user_stated","model_inferred","system"}` 三值契约 + 历史脏值 `"user"` → `"user_stated"` 归一（与 `store::normalize_source` 同口径），其余值 skipped。注释里「跨机保语义」是诉求，但语义的前提就是字段必须落契约。

`mem_export` 返回类型 `MemExportFile` 携带了完整的 `items: Vec<MemExportItem>`（每条 512 维 embedding × 500 条 ≈ 1MB），但前端 `MemoryPanel.tsx:106` 只读 `count`。等于把刚写盘的 JSON 又序列化一份走 IPC 回前端，再丢掉 items。配合 confirmed finding #4 的「回读解析拿报告」双重浪费。修法：函数返回 `MemImportReport` 那种轻量结构（`{ count: usize, exported_at: i64 }`），删除 confirmed finding #4 的回读解析；前端类型签名同步收紧（已是 `{ count: number }`）。

`mem_export` 的 `std::fs::write(&path, &file)` 是非原子写——磁盘满/进程被杀在中途会留下半截 JSON 文件，下次用户误以为导入正常。同 `api_auth.rs` token 持久化先例应该用「写临时文件 → fsync → rename 原子替换」模式（`tempfile::NamedTempFile::new_in(parent).persist(&path)`，或手写 `write + fsync + rename`）。500 条 ≈1MB 的写入通常 <100ms，但用户机器千差万别（网盘同步/磁盘加密/防病毒扫描挂起等场景都能造成 >100ms 卡顿），中途断电很现实。

Stale comment placement — move it to sit directly above `<MemoryPanel />` (or delete it, since `<MemoryPanel />` is self-describing).
